answer.name: Cross-Sectional Momentum
answer.summary: Buy the coins whose 20-day price gain is strongest compared with all other coins.
how_it_works: ts_delta(close, 20) measures how much each coin's price has risen or fallen over the last 20 days.
zscore(...) compares that 20-day gain with the other coins today, so positive scores mean stronger-than-average momentum.
The portfolio favours the highest positive scores, matching a 2-to-4-week holding horizon.
answer.watch_out: This strategy loses money when recent winners suddenly reverse and momentum crashes, especially after sharp market turns.

answer.name: Volume-Confirmed Momentum
answer.summary: Buy the coins with the strongest recent 20-day returns, but only when their trading volume is above its recent average.
how_it_works: ts_sum(returns, 20) adds up the last 20 daily returns to measure recent momentum.
rank(...) compares that momentum across all coins and gives higher scores to the strongest performers.
volume > ts_mean(volume, 20) acts as a filter, so a coin only scores if today’s volume is above its 20-day average.
answer.watch_out: This strategy can lose money when strong recent winners reverse sharply or when a volume spike marks a temporary hype-driven top.

answer.name: Trend-Filtered Momentum Leaders
answer.summary: Buy the stronger-performing coins over the last month, but only if they are also trading above their 30-day average price.
how_it_works: ts_delta(close, 20) measures each coin’s price change over the last 20 days, a medium-term momentum signal.
rank(...) compares that momentum across all coins, so the strongest recent performers get higher scores.
Subtracting 0.5 makes only the top half of momentum-ranked coins score positive.
The close > ts_mean(close, 30) filter keeps a coin only when its price is above its 30-day average, confirming the longer trend is up.
answer.watch_out: This strategy loses money when momentum quickly reverses or choppy markets cause coins to briefly sit above their 30-day average and then fall back.

answer.name: Low-Vol Momentum Rank
answer.summary: Buy coins with strong 20-day returns but lower recent volatility, and stay in USDC when no coin scores above zero.
how_it_works: ts_sum(returns, 20) adds up the last 20 daily returns to measure momentum.
rank(...) turns that momentum into a 0-to-1 cross-sectional score, so stronger coins score higher.
ts_std(returns, 20) measures recent volatility, and rank(...) subtracts a higher penalty for wilder coins.
The final score is positive only when a coin's momentum rank beats its volatility rank.
answer.watch_out: This loses money when markets reverse sharply or when low-volatility coins lag while high-volatility momentum keeps winning.

rank(ts_max(returns, 14)) < 0.9 removes coins in the top 10% of extreme one-day spikes, so lottery-like moves are avoided.

answer.summary: Buy the calmest coins that are not falling, and smooth the signal over a few days to trade less often.
how_it_works: ts_std(returns, 20) measures how volatile each coin has been over the last 20 days.

ts_delta(close, 10) > 0 acts as a filter: the coin only gets a positive score if its price is higher than it was 10 days ago.
ts_mean(..., 5) averages the final score over 5 days so the portfolio changes more slowly and pays fewer fees.
